subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw define a core/plugin-SDK memory provenance and influence-policy contract, or keep this capability in optional memory plugins/MCP integrations while preserving current untrusted framing?
rationale: The choice determines the persistent schema, public plugin boundary, supported backends, operator controls, migration strategy, and security posture; it cannot be safely inferred from an individual feature request.

options.title: Sponsor a shared contract
options.body: Define framework-authenticated origin plus separate review and influence state across the supported memory interfaces, then scope implementation against the canonical provenance work.

options.title: Keep it extension-owned
options.body: Document the existing untrusted framing and route advanced trust lifecycle policies to a plugin or MCP integration that owns its own storage and retrieval contract.

options.title: Adopt a narrow Active Memory exception
options.body: Add only an explicit operator-controlled Active Memory mode while deferring durable cross-backend trust metadata and retrieval policy.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a shared contract
recommendation.body: Define framework-authenticated origin plus separate review and influence state across the supported memory interfaces, then scope implementation against the canonical provenance work.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied prior review already framed the unresolved core security and product boundary and traced the principal memory contracts.
